absent: Locking discipline for virtual processor and control structures
Full memory layout of virtual processor, nested, and control structures
Fast path exit handling and virtual interrupt window setup
Complete exit handler table contents and upper bound
Nested page fault injection and memory management interaction
Timer, interrupt controller, and register emulation details beyond the fragments
Trace, statistics, and userspace exit interfaces

findings.text: Exposes a decision routine that determines whether an exit encountered while running a nested guest should be reflected to the first level hypervisor and, when reflection is chosen, completes the nested exit transition and reports success to the caller.

Exposes a port range checker that consults first level permission maps to decide whether an access should cause an exit to that level, treating out of range ports and unreadable map bytes as reasons to exit.
Exposes a privilege query that reports zero for virtual eight six mode and otherwise derives the level from saved stack segment access rights, with support for bypassing cached state.

Exposes an alignment check policy that allows delivery when split lock detection is unavailable, otherwise only when running at user privilege with alignment checking enabled in both control state and flags.
Exposes a pre emulation gate that requests fault propagation for enclave mode exits and rejects emulation during certain event delivery states, otherwise permitting continuation.
Exposes a predicate that reports whether required emulation cannot be completed because a nested entry is pending or because an exception is outstanding while not in virtual eight six mode.

Central exit dispatcher clears a software virtual interrupt blocked flag after a one second wait with a warning, honors a fast path completion signal, bounds checks the basic reason, optionally handles selected exits directly under speculation mitigation, then clamps the index and invokes the registered handler or falls back to an unexpected exit path.

Nested handling first processes a late entry failure as a reflection, then gives host interest precedence over guest interest, and only when the host declines and the guest requests the exit does it capture interrupt details and qualification and transition to the first level.

Host claims nested exception exits for virtualization faults and non maskable cases, plus alignment checks the guest would not receive, plus host side paging conditions needing interception, plus debug and breakpoint cases when guest debugging uses matching single step or breakpoint modes.

Host retains bus lock and virtual function exits, page modification log full and timer exits, table structure faults and access faults, plus entry time machine checks and external interrupts occurring in a nested guest.
Host claims a nested processor identification exit only when the requested leaf is disallowed for the virtual processor, otherwise leaving the decision to lower level logic.

First level interest in nested exception exits is asserted for paging and non maskable cases and otherwise follows the per vector bitmap. State errors, invalidation without condition, task switch, triple fault, and virtualization instruction operations are always requested.

Many nested exits reach the first level only when its corresponding execution control enables that interception, covering wait and pause styles, monitor and trap flag styles, timestamp and random styles, performance and invalidation styles, plus halt and window styles, with some cases combining two controls.

Nested IO interest without bitmap use follows the unconditional control. With bitmaps it decodes port and width from qualification and scans consecutive bytes, selecting low or high tables by port range with reuse of repeated table bytes.

Nested register interest without bitmap use always exits. With bitmaps the index comes from qualification for immediate forms and from the counter register otherwise, then selects among four quadrants by access kind and high range offset before testing the indexed bit.

Nested control register interest separates move toward, move away, flag clear, and status word store. Moves compare masked values against shadows for two registers and consult load or store controls for two others, with narrow bit handling for the latter operations.

Secure leaf exits depend on host capability, an enable control, and a per leaf map with saturation of large leaves. Control structure accesses without shadowing always exit and otherwise decode the field from instruction details and test a map. Trap exits follow the monitor control or a specific entry encoding.
Interrupt helpers classify paging, virtualization, alignment, breakpoint, and debug conditions by vector, and detect error code presence by requiring both validity and delivery bits.

Invalid state handling loops for a bounded count while emulation remains required, servicing window openings, event requests, single instruction emulation with ordering, unhandleable states, halt requests, and pending guest work before resuming.

External interrupt exits only account statistics. Interrupt window exits clear the window control, request event processing, and account statistics. Preemption timer exits assert nested context and notify the timer model. Immediate register write exits forward qualification and register to emulation.

Extended page table misconfiguration first probes emulatability, then for non nested guests attempts a fast memory mapped shortcut with tracing and skipping, otherwise raises a reserved bit page fault using the faulting physical address.

Instruction emulation inside an enclave cannot use the reported instruction pointer or code stream, so the handler queues an invalid opcode fault to avoid guest denial of service, and emulation during event vectoring is rejected unless explicitly allowed.

Permission checking uses two eight kilobyte ranges split at the midpoint of the sixteen bit port space, with higher ports treated as intercepting, and derives table byte and bit positions from the port value.

Permission map holds four one kilobyte regions ordered by access kind and by low versus high register ranges with the high base at the architected offset, testing the indexed bit when inside range and otherwise requesting an exit.
